texts.facts: (D) That, the Respondents may kindly be directed to Consult the Students/ Representative before taking any decision with regard to Student Issues, specially Food and Transportation. According to the petitioner, the students community of IIT Indore has for the last one and half years continuously lodged complaints via official channels to the concerned authorities at IIT Indore regarding serious problems in quality of food as well as the high prices for food in the mess. To support the aforesaid paper cutting has been filed. It is also alleged that the institute has reduced the number of buses plying to and fro from the campus to parts of Indore city, which particularly impacts the female population and limits their productivity, which is against the spirit of the Justice Verma Committee (Bills of Rights, Part IV - Right to Secured Spaces), UGC and AICTE Regulation.
texts.arguments: The petitioner who is pursuing LLB course has filed this Public Interest Litigation and prayed for the following relief :- "(A) That the Respondents may kindly be directed to provide the Proper Infrastructure, Food Facilities and Transportation facilities to the student of IIT. (B) That the IIT Administration may kindly be directed Give Proper representation to the students in Committee Constituted for the purpose of dealing with Students Issues. (C) That the High Level Committee may kindly be Constituted to hear/inquire the Grievances of the Student and further to provide solution to their genuine problems. Further to appoint a Committee to inquire and take appropriate action against the erring persons responsible for mismanagement and irregularities in the campus. (G) That any other Relief, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit may also kindly given, along with Cost." 2. The students are forced to study in very pathetic condition. Several buildings of the IIT are operating without Fireman's lifts of Fire Safety Centre, which is required under the aegis of National Building Code of India, 2016. The Institution currently operates several committees without adequate student representation in violation of UGC Guidelines and Regulations on the matter. The administration in the utter violation of the UGC Guidelines has not given proper representation to the students in different Committees. Due to delay in construction of the IIT building the students are forced to study in the under constructed building. As per news paper cutting there is mismanagement and irregularities in the IIT Indore and prayed for issuance of proper directions as prayed in para 11 of the writ petition. 4. Per contra, Shri P. Mathur, learned Senior counsel for the respondents No.2 and 3 has submitted that petitioner is misrepresenting this court. The writ petition is based on the false premises. The respondent - Institute is a premier educational Institute of the country having immense reputation globally. The respondent - Institute is efficiently rendering quality services to its students. The Institute never involves in any kind of illegal activities. The petitioner has miserably failed to submit representation / letter to the respondent Institute highlighting his grievance in respect to the allegations raised in the petition; instead the petitioner has directly preferred the present writ petition just to malign the reputation of the Institute. It is submitted that the guidelines issued by the UGC are not binding on the Institute. The respondent - Institute is constantly delivering excellent educational services to the students from across the nation. The writ petition is based on news-paper article containing incorrect and false fact and no effort has been made to verify the facts as mentioned in the said article and prayed for dismissal of the writ petition with exemplary cost. The petitioner is a law student, he has not filed any document to substantiate his grievance made in the writ petition. Courts of justice should not be allowed to be polluted by unscrupulous Harsh Wardhan Sharma vs Union Of India on 13 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79170483/ 3 litigants by resorting to the extraordinary jurisdiction.
